formalization.definitions:
namespace PV

/-- Terms of the base sort `{0,1}^*`, built from variables, the primitive
constants/functions of PV (`ε`, successors `s0,s1`, concatenation `cat`,
smash `smash`, trim-right `tr`, iterated trim `itr`), and applications of
arbitrary named PV function symbols (`app name args`), which covers all
functions introduced by composition or limited recursion on notation. -/
inductive Term : Type
  | var : ℕ → Term
  | eps : Term
  | s0 : Term → Term
  | s1 : Term → Term
  | cat : Term → Term → Term
  | smash : Term → Term → Term
  | tr : Term → Term
  | itr : Term → Term → Term
  | app : String → List Term → Term

/-- Convenience: `succ i t` is `s1 t` if `i = true` and `s0 t` if `i = false`,
used to uniformly range over `i ∈ {0,1}`. -/
def Term.succ (i : Bool) (t : Term) : Term := cond i (Term.s1 t) (Term.s0 t)

/-- Simultaneous substitution of terms for variables. -/
def Term.subst (σ : ℕ → Term) : Term → Term
  | Term.var n => σ n
  | Term.eps => Term.eps
  | Term.s0 t => Term.s0 (t.subst σ)
  | Term.s1 t => Term.s1 (t.subst σ)
  | Term.cat t1 t2 => Term.cat (t1.subst σ) (t2.subst σ)
  | Term.smash t1 t2 => Term.smash (t1.subst σ) (t2.subst σ)
  | Term.tr t => Term.tr (t.subst σ)
  | Term.itr t1 t2 => Term.itr (t1.subst σ) (t2.subst σ)
  | Term.app f args => Term.app f (args.map (fun t => t.subst σ))

/-- `Deriv t1 t2` means `PV ⊢ t1 = t2`: the equational derivability relation
of Cook's PV, generated by reflexivity (L0), symmetry (L1), transitivity (L2),
congruence (L3), substitution (L4), the defining axioms of `cat, tr, itr,
smash`, and the (single-variable) structural-induction rule. -/
inductive Deriv : Term → Term → Prop
  | refl (t : Term) : Deriv t t
  | symm {t1 t2 : Term} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv t2 t1
  | trans {t1 t2 t3 : Term} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv t2 t3 → Deriv t1 t3
  | congr_s0 {t t' : Term} : Deriv t t' → Deriv (Term.s0 t) (Term.s0 t')
  | congr_s1 {t t' : Term} : Deriv t t' → Deriv (Term.s1 t) (Term.s1 t')
  | congr_cat {t1 t1' t2 t2' : Term} :
      Deriv t1 t1' → Deriv t2 t2' → Deriv (Term.cat t1 t2) (Term.cat t1' t2')
  | congr_smash {t1 t1' t2 t2' : Term} :
      Deriv t1 t1' → Deriv t2 t2' → Deriv (Term.smash t1 t2) (Term.smash t1' t2')
  | congr_tr {t t' : Term} : Deriv t t' → Deriv (Term.tr t) (Term.tr t')
  | congr_itr {t1 t1' t2 t2' : Term} :
      Deriv t1 t1' → Deriv t2 t2' → Deriv (Term.itr t1 t2) (Term.itr t1' t2')
  | congr_app (f : String) {args args' : List Term} :
      List.Forall₂ Deriv args args' → Deriv (Term.app f args) (Term.app f args')
  | subst (σ : ℕ → Term) {t1 t2 : Term} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv (t1.subst σ) (t2.subst σ)
  | ax_cat_eps (x : Term) : Deriv (Term.cat x Term.eps) x
  | ax_cat_s0 (x y : Term) : Deriv (Term.cat x (Term.s0 y)) (Term.s0 (Term.cat x y))
  | ax_cat_s1 (x y : Term) : Deriv (Term.cat x (Term.s1 y)) (Term.s1 (Term.cat x y))
  | ax_tr_eps : Deriv (Term.tr Term.eps) Term.eps
  | ax_tr_s0 (x : Term) : Deriv (Term.tr (Term.s0 x)) x
  | ax_tr_s1 (x : Term) : Deriv (Term.tr (Term.s1 x)) x
  | ax_itr_eps (x : Term) : Deriv (Term.itr x Term.eps) x
  | ax_itr_s0 (x y : Term) : Deriv (Term.itr x (Term.s0 y)) (Term.tr (Term.itr x y))
  | ax_itr_s1 (x y : Term) : Deriv (Term.itr x (Term.s1 y)) (Term.tr (Term.itr x y))
  | ax_smash_eps (x : Term) : Deriv (Term.smash x Term.eps) Term.eps
  | ax_smash_s0 (x y : Term) : Deriv (Term.smash x (Term.s0 y)) (Term.cat x (Term.smash x y))
  | ax_smash_s1 (x y : Term) : Deriv (Term.smash x (Term.s1 y)) (Term.cat x (Term.smash x y))
  | ind (f1 f2 g h0 h1 : String) (xs : List Term) (y : Term) :
      Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.eps])) (Term.app g xs) →
      Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.eps])) (Term.app g xs) →
      Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.s0 y])) (Term.app h0 (xs ++ [y, Term.app f1 (xs ++ [y])])) →
      Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.s0 y])) (Term.app h0 (xs ++ [y, Term.app f2 (xs ++ [y])])) →
      Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.s1 y])) (Term.app h1 (xs ++ [y, Term.app f1 (xs ++ [y])])) →
      Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.s1 y])) (Term.app h1 (xs ++ [y, Term.app f2 (xs ++ [y])])) →
      Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [y])) (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [y]))

end PV

    (hbase00_2 : Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.eps, Term.eps])) (Term.app g00 xs))
    (hbase01_1 : ∀ (y : Term) (i : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.eps, Term.succ i y])) (Term.app g01 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y])))
    (hbase01_2 : ∀ (y : Term) (i : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.eps, Term.succ i y])) (Term.app g01 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y])))
    (hbase10_1 : ∀ (y : Term) (i : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y, Term.eps])) (Term.app g10 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y])))
    (hbase10_2 : ∀ (y : Term) (i : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y, Term.eps])) (Term.app g10 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y])))
    (hind1 : ∀ (y1 y2 : Term) (i1 i2 : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.succ i1 y1, Term.succ i2 y2]))
              (Term.app (h i1 i2) (xs ++ [y1, y2, Term.app f1 (xs ++ [y1, y2])])))
    (hind2 : ∀ (y1 y2 : Term) (i1 i2 : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.succ i1 y1, Term.succ i2 y2]))
              (Term.app (h i1 i2) (xs ++ [y1, y2, Term.app f2 (xs ++ [y1, y2])])))
    (y1 y2 : Term) :
    Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [y1, y2])) (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [y1, y2]))
formalization.notes: `Term` is the syntax of PV terms over `{0,1}^*`, with variables, the primitive symbols `ε, s0, s1, cat (∘), smash (#), tr (TR), itr (ITR)`, and a generic `app name args` node standing for application of any PV function symbol (covering all functions obtained by composition or limited recursion on notation, since the theorem only uses their defining equations, not how they were introduced). `Deriv t1 t2` formalizes `PV ⊢ t1 = t2` via the rules L0–L4 (`refl, symm, trans`, the `congr_*` constructors, and `subst`), the twelve defining axioms of `cat, tr, itr, smash`, and the single-variable structural-induction rule `ind`, exactly as stated in the setting. In the theorem, the shared parameter `xs` plays the role of `\vec x` (same vector throughout all hypotheses and the conclusion); `Term.succ i t` uniformly represents `s_i(t)` for `i ∈ {0,1}` encoded as `Bool`. The six hypothesis groups correspond exactly to the four bullet points of the statement (with `j ∈ {1,2}` unrolled into the two named hypotheses `..._1`/`..._2`, and the universal quantifiers over `y`, `i`, `y1, y2`, `i1, i2` made explicit `∀`-binders inside each hypothesis, since these schemas must hold for all values, not just the ones occurring in the conclusion); `h : Bool → Bool → String` packages the four functions `h_{i1 i2}`. The conclusion `Deriv (app f1 (xs ++ [y1,y2])) (app f2 (xs ++ [y1,y2]))` is exactly `PV ⊢ f1(\vec x,y1,y2) = f2(\vec x,y1,y2)`, universally quantified over `y1, y2` as theorem parameters.
formalization.readback:
The following statement is literally asserted by the Lean declaration `ind_multiple_var`:

Let $ \mathcal{X} $ be a list of terms $ \text{xs} $, and let $ f_1, f_2, g_{00}, g_{01}, g_{10} $ be strings, and let $ h : \{0,1\} \times \{0,1\} \to \{ \text{strings} \} $ be a function from pairs of booleans to strings. Suppose the following derivability conditions hold:

- $ \text{Deriv}( \text{app } f_1 ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{eps}, \text{eps}] ) , \text{app } g_{00} \text{xs} ) $,
- $ \text{Deriv}( \text{app } f_2 ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{eps}, \text{eps}] ) , \text{app } g_{00} \text{xs} ) $,
- For all terms $ y $ and all booleans $ i $, $ \text{Deriv}( \text{app } f_1 ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{eps}, \text{succ } i y] ) , \text{app } g_{01} ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{succ } i y] ) ) $,
- For all terms $ y $ and all booleans $ i $, $ \text{Deriv}( \text{app } f_2 ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{eps}, \text{succ } i y] ) , \text{app } g_{01} ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{succ } i y] ) ) $,
- For all terms $ y $ and all booleans $ i $, $ \text{Deriv}( \text{app } f_1 ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{succ } i y, \text{eps}] ) , \text{app } g_{10} ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{succ } i y] ) ) $,
- For all terms $ y $ and all booleans $ i $, $ \text{Deriv}( \text{app } f_2 ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{succ } i y, \text{eps}] ) , \text{app } g_{10} ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{succ } i y] ) ) $,
- For all terms $ y_1, y_2 $ and all booleans $ i_1, i_2 $, $ \text{Deriv}( \text{app } f_1 ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{succ } i_1 y_1, \text{succ } i_2 y_2] ) , \text{app } h(i_1, i_2) ( \text{xs} ++ [y_1, y_2, \text{app } f_1 ( \text{xs} ++ [y_1, y_2] ) ] ) ) $,
- For all terms $ y_1, y_2 $ and all booleans $ i_1, i_2 $, $ \text{Deriv}( \text{app } f_2 ( \text{xs} ++ [\text{succ } i_1 y_1, \text{succ } i_2 y_2] ) , \text{app } h(i_1, i_2) ( \text{xs} ++ [y_1, y_2, \text{app } f_2 ( \text{xs} ++ [y_1, y_2] ) ] ) ) $.

Then, for any terms $ y_1, y_2 $, it follows that:

$$
\text{Deriv}( \text{app } f_1 ( \text{xs} ++ [y_1, y_2] ) , \text{app } f_2 ( \text{xs} ++ [y_1, y_2] ) )
$$

This holds for all such $ y_1, y_2 $, and all $ \text{xs} $, $ f_1, f_2, g_{00}, g_{01}, g_{10} $, and $ h $ satisfying the above conditions.
formalization.issues:
None. Checking point by point:

- All four families of hypotheses (base case at (ε,ε); base cases at (ε, sᵢy) and (sᵢy, ε) for both bits i; inductive step at (s_{i1}y1, s_{i2}y2) for both bit pairs) are present for both j=1 and j=2, matching the source exactly, including that g01/g10 are applied to the full successor term s_i(y) (not to y and i separately) and that h_{i1i2} is applied to y1, y2 (not to their successors) together with the recursive call f_j(x,y1,y2), exactly as in the source.
- The apparent reuse of the letter "j" in the source's "for j ∈ {0,1}" (as opposed to the outer j ∈ {1,2} indexing f_j) is correctly disambiguated in Lean via a separate Bool variable `i`, which is the only sensible reading since s_j is only defined for bit values.
- The conclusion matches: Deriv (f1 applied to xs++[y1,y2]) (f2 applied to xs++[y1,y2]), universally quantified over y1, y2, mirroring "PV ⊢ f1(x,y1,y2) = f2(x,y1,y2)".
- `xs : List Term` faithfully represents the vector x̄ of arbitrary arity, and all functions (f1, f2, g00, g01, g10, h_{i1i2}) are represented as arbitrary named PV function symbols via `Term.app`, consistent with the setting's description of functions introduced by composition/limited recursion on notation; the theorem does not need to reprove that these symbols are well-formed PV functions, since its proof (per the informal proof) only uses the stated equational facts, the equational calculus, and the structural induction rule.
- The `Deriv` relation's axioms for cat, tr, itr, smash exactly match the source's defining axioms (x∘ε=x, x∘s_i(y)=s_i(x∘y), TR(ε)=ε, TR(s_i(x))=x, ITR(x,ε)=x, ITR(x,s_i(y))=TR(ITR(x,y)), x#ε=ε, x#s_i(y)=x∘(x#y)), and L0–L4 are represented by refl/symm/trans/congr_*/subst. The `ind` constructor correctly encodes the single-variable structural-induction rule used as a primitive derivation rule of PV (required background machinery, not the theorem itself), matching the source's rule with base case g and branch functions h0, h1 for both f1 and f2.
- No hypothesis is missing, weakened, or vacuously trivial, and no extra hypothesis is added; the universal quantification over y, y1, y2, i, i1, i2 in the hypotheses and over y1, y2 in the conclusion correctly mirrors the source's "for all" / free-variable conventions.

sketch.main_proof:
have hdiag :=
  key_diag xs f1 f2 g00 g01 g10 h
    hbase00_1 hbase00_2 hbase01_1 hbase01_2 hbase10_1 hbase10_2 hind1 hind2
    y1 y2 (Term.cat y1 y2)
have hself : Deriv (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) (Term.cat y1 y2)) Term.eps :=
  itr_self_trim (Term.cat y1 y2)
have hA : Deriv (Term.itr y1 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) (Term.cat y1 y2))) y1 :=
  Deriv.trans (Deriv.congr_itr (Deriv.refl y1) hself) (Deriv.ax_itr_eps y1)
have hB : Deriv (Term.itr y2 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) (Term.cat y1 y2))) y2 :=
  Deriv.trans (Deriv.congr_itr (Deriv.refl y2) hself) (Deriv.ax_itr_eps y2)
have e1 :
    Deriv
      (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.itr y1 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) (Term.cat y1 y2)),
                            Term.itr y2 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) (Term.cat y1 y2))]))
      (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [y1, y2])) :=
  congr_app_two xs f1 _ y1 _ y2 hA hB
have e2 :
    Deriv
      (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.itr y1 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) (Term.cat y1 y2)),
                            Term.itr y2 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) (Term.cat y1 y2))]))
      (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [y1, y2])) :=
  congr_app_two xs f2 _ y1 _ y2 hA hB
exact Deriv.trans (Deriv.trans (Deriv.symm e1) hdiag) e2

lemmas.name: congr_app_two
lemmas.statement:
theorem congr_app_two (xs : List Term) (f : String) (a a' b b' : Term)
    (ha : Deriv a a') (hb : Deriv b b') :
    Deriv (Term.app f (xs ++ [a, b])) (Term.app f (xs ++ [a', b']))
lemmas.proof:
apply Deriv.congr_app
induction xs with
| nil =>
  exact List.Forall₂.cons ha (List.Forall₂.cons hb List.Forall₂.nil)
| cons x xs' ih =>
  exact List.Forall₂.cons (Deriv.refl x) ih

lemmas.name: key_diag
lemmas.statement:
theorem key_diag
    (xs : List Term)
    (f1 f2 g00 g01 g10 : String) (h : Bool → Bool → String)
    (hbase00_1 : Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.eps, Term.eps])) (Term.app g00 xs))
    (hbase00_2 : Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.eps, Term.eps])) (Term.app g00 xs))
    (hbase01_1 : ∀ (y : Term) (i : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.eps, Term.succ i y])) (Term.app g01 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y])))
    (hbase01_2 : ∀ (y : Term) (i : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.eps, Term.succ i y])) (Term.app g01 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y])))
    (hbase10_1 : ∀ (y : Term) (i : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y, Term.eps])) (Term.app g10 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y])))
    (hbase10_2 : ∀ (y : Term) (i : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y, Term.eps])) (Term.app g10 (xs ++ [Term.succ i y])))
    (hind1 : ∀ (y1 y2 : Term) (i1 i2 : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.succ i1 y1, Term.succ i2 y2]))
              (Term.app (h i1 i2) (xs ++ [y1, y2, Term.app f1 (xs ++ [y1, y2])])))
    (hind2 : ∀ (y1 y2 : Term) (i1 i2 : Bool),
        Deriv (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.succ i1 y1, Term.succ i2 y2]))
              (Term.app (h i1 i2) (xs ++ [y1, y2, Term.app f2 (xs ++ [y1, y2])])))
    (y1 y2 w2 : Term) :
    Deriv
      (Term.app f1 (xs ++ [Term.itr y1 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) w2), Term.itr y2 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) w2)]))
      (Term.app f2 (xs ++ [Term.itr y1 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) w2), Term.itr y2 (Term.itr (Term.cat y1 y2) w2)]))
